author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:

  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected
summary: A booked visit can be corrected afterwards. The correction replaces that visit's date and description, is held to the same rules as booking, and leaves the pet's visit count unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when its correction is begun, then the visit's current date and description are offered for changing.
Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown.
Given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet has the same number of visits as before.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the description is named.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the date is named.
Given a refused correction, when it is presented again, then it carries the values that were submitted.
Given a visit that does not belong to the named pet and owner, when its correction is attempted, then it is refused.
non_goals: cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4)
a link to the correction form from the owner detail page
correcting any visit detail other than the date and the description
notes: NG-5 narrowed to cancellation alone; recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-17-non-goal-visit-correction.md. Two narrowest-reading choices are recorded as open questions in the PRD rather than decided here: no visible entry point (owner deferred it to a follow-up request), and a past-dated visit cannot keep its date through a correction because the future-date rule applies unchanged. Criterion 7 follows the existing Visits edge case 1, which already refuses a booking against a pet that is not the named owner's.

  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The correction reuses the visit-booking shape in the owner feature package unchanged: a second GET/POST pair on VisitController under the existing /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits path, the same createOrUpdateVisitForm template, and the same Owner-rooted write path (system-design.md#contracts, Invariants the rows cannot carry). Two small adjustments make it fit. First, VisitController's shared @ModelAttribute('visit') fabricates a fresh Visit and attaches it to the pet on every request into the controller; the correction route must resolve the existing visit instead, so the method takes an optional visitId path variable and branches. Second, Pet gains an identity lookup over its visits, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) - recorded in system-design.md as: a visit is reached by identity through its pet, as a pet is through its owner. No new module, pattern, dependency, or ADR: the product decision narrowing NG-5 is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-17-non-goal-visit-correction.md.
integration_points: VisitController gains a GET and a POST on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit; no navigation links to it (declared non-goal)
loadPetWithVisit resolves the visit from the pet when a visitId is present and creates one otherwise; the created-visit branch must stay unreachable on the edit routes
Pet exposes a by-identity visit lookup used by the controller; Visit's own accessors are unchanged
OwnerRepository.save(owner) cascades the merge of the mutated visit - Owner and Pet both map their collections CascadeType.ALL with eager fetch, so no new persistence wiring appears

patterns.description: the existing init/process edit pair nested under an owner: GET renders the shared create-or-update form, POST validates and redirects to the owner page
getPet(Integer) - the aggregate's by-identity child lookup returning null when the child does not belong to it; the visit lookup mirrors it
the non-future-date rejection that criterion 5 reuses verbatim; extracting it to one private method keeps booking and correction on a single rule
the IllegalArgumentException raised when the pet does not belong to the named owner; criterion 7 is the same refusal one level down, raised when the visit does not belong to the named pet

risks.risk: The shared @ModelAttribute('visit') runs before every handler in VisitController. If the edit routes fall through to the new-Visit branch, pet.addVisit attaches a phantom visit that OwnerRepository.save cascades, breaking criterion 3 (visit count unchanged) while every other criterion still passes.
risks.mitigation: Bind the submitted values onto the instance the lookup returned - never onto a fresh one - and cover it with the count assertion named in test_names (theCorrectedPetShouldKeepTheSameNumberOfVisits).

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002 forbids hard-coded user-facing text and partly translated wording; a build test compares keys across all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages. New button or heading wording for the correction form fails that test unless every bundle carries it.
risks.mitigation: The narrowest reading needs no new wording: the template already branches on visit['new'] for its heading, and no acceptance criterion asks for different button text. If wording is added anyway, add the key to all eleven bundles in the same change.

risks.risk: The correction mutates a detached entity in place, so a refused submission leaves the bound values on the in-memory visit.
risks.mitigation: No flush can occur - spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled and the error path skips save - so the refusal re-renders the submitted values (criterion 6) without touching the database. Assert the refusal with a repository read, not with the model object.

risks.risk: Every mutating route in this application is unauthenticated and CSRF-unprotected (system-design.md#security-context). The correction route adds one more.
risks.mitigation: Consistent with the recorded demonstration posture; no new trust boundary is introduced. The owner/pet/visit ownership check is the only access control the slice can carry, and criterion 7 requires it.

notes: Verdict basis is grep and direct file reads, not the IDE oracle (not connected in this dispatch) - the weaker basis. Design writes: docs/system-design.md Contracts rows for Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController now carry REQ-VISITEDIT-001, and the aggregate-navigation invariant gained one sentence. Vocabulary: the record is a Visit and its date is the visit date (docs/ubiquitous-language.md); avoid Appointment and Booking in code and page text. Edge case 5 in the PRD is a deliberate consequence, not a defect to design around: a past-dated visit cannot keep its date through a correction.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: no OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured in build.gradle and this reviewer has no network access. The change adds no dependency (build.gradle is not in the change set), so the resolved set is unchanged from the last pass; a human or CI still owns the standing NVD check for Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its managed Jackson.

POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner without @Valid and then calls owners.save(owner), so submitted parameters named firstName, lastName, address, city, or telephone bind onto the loaded owner and are persisted alongside the visit correction, skipping the owner's bean-validation constraints. Identifier binding is blocked by the binder, so this is not weaker than the baseline: processNewVisitForm has exactly the same shape today, and the application has no authentication by design (docs/system-design.md Security Context). Recorded as a standing pattern worth narrowing project-wide (e.g. binding the owner without request-parameter binding), not as a defect this slice introduced.
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization on the new routes: loadPetWithVisit re-resolves owner -> pet -> visit from the repository on every request and rejects a visitId that is not on the named pet (VisitController.java:82-91), so a correction cannot reach another pet's or owner's visit. This satisfies the 'trusting cross-request state' row of docs/security-principles.md - no identifier is trusted because an earlier request validated it.

Mass assignment: the controller's existing @InitBinder setAllowedFields disallows 'id' and '*.id' (VisitController.java:53-56) and covers the two new handlers, so the correction POST cannot rebind a visit, pet, or owner identifier. The new form binds onto the loaded booked visit rather than a detached instance, so no extra visit is created.

Input validation: the future-date rule is applied identically to booking and correction through the extracted rejectDateNotInFuture (VisitController.java:153-156), and @Valid still drives the Visit bean-validation constraints on the correction path - the new route inherits no weaker validation than the booking route.

XSS: no template changed; createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders visit fields through th:text/th:field with Thymeleaf default escaping intact and the form posts to the current URL, so the edit route needs no new markup.

Error handling: the new IllegalArgumentException message carries only path-derived integers (petId, visitId), which Spring converts before the handler runs. No credential, connection string, or user-supplied text can reach the error page through it.

Pattern consistency: Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors the existing Owner.getPet(Integer) lookup, including the isNew() guard and the null-safe Objects.equals comparison. No divergent implementation of an already-secured concern.

No new attack surface classes: the diff adds no file I/O, no process execution, no deserialization, no reflection, no logging of request data, and no dependency change (build.gradle untouched). Pattern sweep over the owner package for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec/JsonTypeInfo/enableDefaultTyping//tmp//System.out returned nothing.

blast_radius.note: One module and nine files: fifteen added lines on Pet, fifty-two on VisitController, the rest tests and docs. semantic_surprise.note: The correction POST takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner without @Valid and then calls owners.save(owner), so firstName, lastName, address, city and telephone submitted to the visit-edit URL bind onto the loaded owner and persist unvalidated alongside the date and description. Identifier binding is blocked by the controller's @InitBinder and processNewVisitForm has the identical shape today, so this is a second instance of an accepted pattern rather than a new weakness, but a URL whose stated job is correcting a visit's date and description also rewriting the owner's address is not what the diff advertises. test_adequacy.note: Eight new tests assert real outcomes rather than restating the implementation, and the count-invariance and elapsed-date cases genuinely pin the two behaviors most likely to break. The gap is durability: owners is a MockitoBean and no test verifies save, while the success assertions read the in-memory visit that data binding mutated, so an implementation that dropped this.owners.save(owner) would still redirect and still pass every assertion. The existing booking tests share that gap, so this is house style, not a regression.
